title: Modular Thrift Profiles: phased rollouts for batching, KV-prefetch, and micro-quant
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Objective: Deliver a repeatable initiative that standardizes 'thrift profiles' — pre-defined configuration bundles combining batching heuristics, KV-prefetch TTLs, and micro-quantization parameters — and roll them out via canary experiments to reduce per-token cost by 10–25% on targeted workloads without >5% quality regression.

Scope:
- Define 3 modular thrift profiles (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with concrete knobs for: dynamic batching window, prefix/KV prefetch TTLs, quantization recipe (bits/format), and fallback rules.
- Implement a canary orchestration plan in Console to assign profiles by route and measure both cost and quality metrics.
- Add observability: cost-per-request, latency P50/P95, generation-quality deltas (BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and prompt-set evals), and safety/semantics regression signals.
- Create rollout playbooks, rollback triggers, and guardrails (e.g., automatic fallback to baseline model for >5% quality regression or >15% latency spike).

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary runs for 2 independent customer-like workloads for 2 weeks with automated monitoring and alerting.
- Achieve >=10% token-econ improvements on one workload and >=6% on the other with quality regressions within the accepted thresholds.
- Runbook and Console controls exist to schedule a staged rollout and perform instant rollback.

Success metrics:
- Primary: percent reduction in cost-per-1000-tokens for covered routes.
- Secondary: no more than 5% increase in policy/QA regressions and maintain P95 latency within 1.2x of baseline.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Aggressive quantization may surface edge-case hallucinations on long-context prompts; we will gate Aggressive on workload fingerprints.
- Batching windows reduce latency sensitivity; we will avoid batching on routes with strict low-latency SLAs.
- Prefetch TTLs increase memory/KV cache churn; need kernel-scheduling changes from ENG to avoid OOM spikes.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0 (spec): finalize profile definitions and required observability signals.
- Week 1–2 (eng implementation): gating flags + Console controls + dashboards.
- Week 3 (internal canary): run on internal test harness using two synthetic workloads and iterate profile defaults.
- Week 4–6 (customer canary): opt-in limited customers (2) with pre-signed agreements and monitoring.
- Week 7 (evaluate): decide go/no-go for wider rollout and prepare runbook.

Stakeholders: PM (Sana), Eng leads (serving runtime: Priya Rao, infra: Miguel Alvarez), Design (Avery Chen — controls UX for Console), Observability (Dana O'Neill).
